squirrel-removal.intro: Donalds is a small Abbeville County town in the rolling piedmont — a compact community of older homes along a few streets, standing in farm and timber country where the woods reach most back fences. Its squirrel work is the small-town version at its simplest: gray squirrels in the attics of the pre-war homes, travelling the street trees and the power lines, chewing in at the eaves and gable vents that a century of weather has softened. In a town Donalds' size, the squirrel population and the housing stock are both small and both known — the same colonies work the same streets, and a house that gets sealed properly tends to stay sealed, because there are only so many roofs to rotate among.
squirrel-removal.extendedBody:
Small town, complete roofline

The Donalds job is thoroughness at small scale: the whole roofline read — eaves, gables, chimney flashing, the junctions where the porch roofs meet the walls — the squirrels excluded with one-way devices, and every opening rebuilt in metal rather than patched in kind. Gray squirrels chew; a patch of matching material is a door with a timer on it. The street trees overhanging the older homes are mapped for the cuts that break the bridge, and the attic is checked for the nest material and wiring damage a colony leaves behind. What makes the work hold in a town like Donalds is that the rotation is finite: with every structure on the parcel read — the barn and the well house included, since a squirrel evicted from the attic tests them the same week — the animals run out of indoor options on the property, and the woods behind the fence are where they belonged in the first place.

faqs.q: How much does squirrel removal cost in Donalds?
faqs.a: It depends on the entries and the attic — most Donalds homes are a compact, complete job: exclusion, metal sealing across the roofline, and the attic checked. We inspect first and quote firmly before work starts, so the number covers the whole roof rather than the first hole found. If the barn or an outbuilding is part of the squirrels' rotation, we will say so and quote it in the same visit rather than discovering it on a second call.

faqs.q: We hear running in our Donalds attic in the mornings. Is it definitely squirrels?
faqs.a: Morning and late-afternoon running, with rolling and chewing sounds, is the gray squirrel signature — they are daytime animals on a commuter's schedule. Night noise points elsewhere: flying squirrels, rats, or a raccoon. The distinction matters because the entries differ — squirrels chew in at the roofline in daylight-sized holes — and the inspection confirms which animal you have by the sign before we quote anything. We would rather identify it free of assumptions on the first visit than exclude the wrong tenant.
